subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency for Finly streaming UX
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir@finly.com>, Priya Desai <priya@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency for Finly streaming UX

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call to make sure we captured your priorities and next steps. If anything below is off, please correct and I’ll update the MAP.

Summary / pain points you shared:
- Production streaming experience: users are seeing choppy token-by-token rendering when model responses hit ~350-500 tokens; UX degrades for long responses.
- P95 latency targets: business wants p95 generation latency <= 350ms for the common 128-256 token replies and <= 800ms for longer 512+ token streams.
- Concurrency: peak traffic is ~220 concurrent active sessions during market open; plan for 3x buffer for spikes (~660).
- Cost sensitivity: current per-token spend is ~60% of infra budget for inference - you want predictable unit economics before GA.
- Reliability: fallback behavior required when capacity is constrained (graceful degrade to smaller model variants).

Current stack (as discussed):
- Frontend: React SPA with server-side event (SSE) streaming to render tokens.
- Backend: EKS-managed services, inference currently on GPU instances via a third-party managed endpoint.
- Traffic pattern: bursty with heavy spikes 09:30-10:30 ET; 30-40% of requests are long streams (>512 tokens).

Success criteria (what would make this a win):
- Meet p95 latency <= 350ms for typical responses (128-256 tokens) while supporting streaming UX without perceptible lag.
- Support sustained 220+ concurrent streams with headroom for 3x spikes.
- Demonstrated 20-30% improvement in per-token cost or comparable unit economics with predictable billing.
- Clear rollout plan (canary -> prod) with rollback behavior and audit logs.

Next steps / action items:
1) We’ll share a one-page MAP + proposed sizing and cost estimate (attached). [Attachment: redwood_discovery_recap_finly_20261205.pdf]
2) Tech deep-dive with Aditya + Finly infra team next week to validate traffic traces and token distributions. You mentioned Mon/Tue next week morning ET; please share availability.
3) We'll spin up a short proof-of-concept run: 2 hours of 3x-concurrency stress test and a streaming UX pass.
4) Procurement: I’ll include a preliminary SOW and pricing in the MAP for internal review.

Open questions for you:
- Can you share a sample traffic trace (anonymized) showing request size distribution and inter-arrival times?
- Any regulatory/data-residency constraints for models/chat logs?

Attachments: redwood_discovery_recap_finly_20261205.pdf, mutual_action_plan_FIN-2026-042.xlsx

Thanks - happy to sync on edits.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: p95 latency & concurrency for Finly streaming UX

Thanks Marissa - really appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- p95 targets: the <=350ms number is for our synchronous quick-reply flows (~128 tokens). For long-form summaries (512+ tokens) we care more about steady token arrival rate (no >400ms token gaps) than total generation time.
- Concurrency: 220 is current baseline; spikes have gone up to ~480 in the last three weeks (market volatility). 3x buffer sounds safe for planning.
- Stack detail: we call out that some traffic must remain on-prem for compliance (EU customers), but the primary workload is US cloud.

I can share a redacted trace and our traffic histogram - attaching now.

Samir
Product Lead, Finly
samir@finly.com

Looping in a few technical follow-ups from my side after reviewing the trace Samir attached:

- Token distribution looks heavier on long responses than initially estimated (20-25% > 512 tokens). For streaming UX we’ll want to optimize for steady per-token latency (we typically aim for <120ms per token at p50 and <400ms at p95 for streaming workloads on our optimized runtime).
- We'll propose a reference deployment: 4 dedicated GPU pods (A100 equivalent) behind a continuous-batching router + KV cache for common prefixes. That should meet your p95 targets at baseline and allow 3x spike handling with autoscale.
- Need Finly to share: a) sample auth token flow for staged environment, b) expected retention window for KV cache (if you want contextual continuity across sessions).

I can prep a short demo of our streaming behavior (token pacing + SSE) - suggest Tue 12/8 10:00-11:00 ET. Marissa / Ethan, can you confirm?

-Aditya
